context:
1. In tests/conftest.py, add after existing imports:
   - _TEST_LOCK_PATH = Path.home() / ".benchbox" / "test.lock"
   - _test_lock_fd: int | None = None  (module-level, keeps fd alive)
   - _should_acquire_test_lock(config) helper function
   - pytest_configure hook: acquires fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB), writes
     PID+timestamp+cmd to lock file, stores fd in _test_lock_fd
   - pytest_unconfigure hook: releases lock via flock(LOCK_UN) and closes fd

2. Error message format when blocked:
   "[benchbox] BLOCKED: A parallel test run is already active.
     Lock file : ~/.benchbox/test.lock
     Holder    : pid:XXXX started:YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS cmd:...
     Options:
       • Wait for the other run to finish and retry.
       • Run single-threaded (no lock):  pytest -n 0 ...
       • Bypass lock (dangerous):         BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK=1 pytest ..."

3. In Makefile, add test-unlock convenience target after test-fast:
   test-unlock:
       @echo "Removing stale BenchBox test lock..."
       @rm -f ~/.benchbox/test.lock
       @echo "Lock cleared."
description:
pytest.ini defaults to `-n auto`, which spawns one worker per logical CPU (10 on
this machine). When two agent sessions each trigger `make test-fast`, the result is
20+ concurrent pytest workers competing for CPU, bringing the machine to a halt.

Add an exclusive `fcntl.flock` lock in `tests/conftest.py` so that only one
parallel test run can be active at a time. A second concurrent attempt fails
immediately with a clear, actionable error message identifying the lock holder.

Chosen approach: `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` on `~/.benchbox/test.lock`.
The OS auto-releases the lock when the holder process dies (no stale lock cleanup
needed). No new dependencies - `fcntl` is stdlib on macOS/Linux.

anti_patterns.dont: add lock logic to production benchbox source
anti_patterns.why: scope is tests/ and Makefile only

anti_patterns.dont: store lock metadata in _test_lock_fd write until after flock succeeds
anti_patterns.why: ftruncate/write must happen only after exclusive lock is confirmed
they add dependencies; fcntl is stdlib and sufficient for macOS/Linux

use pytest_configure instead. Reason: numprocesses is readable from config.option at configure time (post CLI parse, pre session); sessionstart is too late and the lock would not block workers from being spawned

preserves.behavior: All 13,000+ fast-marked tests continue to pass after the hooks are added - confirm with `make test-fast` reporting 13052 passed
CI pipelines: lock is user-local (~/.benchbox/test.lock); CI containers with fresh filesystems must never see a pre-existing lock
Crash recovery: after kill -9 on a running test session, the next invocation must succeed without any manual cleanup (OS auto-releases flock on exit)
Single-threaded runs: numprocesses == 0 or None must bypass the lock entirely
xdist workers: hasattr(config, 'workerinput') check must prevent workers from competing for the lock - only the controller process acquires it

verifications.command: make test-fast & sleep 5 && make test-fast 2>&1; echo "exit:$?"
verifications.description: Second concurrent parallel run is blocked with exit code 1 and BLOCKED message
Single-threaded run is never blocked (no lock acquired)
verifications.expected: tests pass with no BLOCKED message

verifications.description: Env-var bypass allows concurrent parallel runs

verifications.command: make test-fast & sleep 3 && kill -9 $! ; sleep 1 && make test-fast 2>&1 | tail -3
verifications.description: After a crashed run (kill -9), the next parallel run succeeds without manual cleanup
verifications.expected: tests pass (OS auto-released flock on kill)
